_comment: PROVENANCE + INVESTIGATIONS overlay for the ws-surgery.js decision engine. This file adds NOTHING to the clinical decision: the emergency flag, management ladder, source control, referral, clinical notes and empiric antibiotic regimens all come from ws-surgery.js and have exactly one home. What lives here is (a) the source attribution that engine file does not carry per-syndrome, (b) an INVESTIGATE band the engine does not model, and (c) deep links into the existing StewardMD Calculators module. Reviewed separately from the engine; review.status governs whether it renders.

sources.title: Guidelines for the management of intra-abdominal infections

investigate.text: Urine or serum beta-hCG in every woman of childbearing age, before imaging and before theatre.
FBC, U&E, LFT, amylase or lipase, CRP, lactate, group and save. Lactate is a resuscitation marker, not a diagnostic test.
Erect chest radiograph for free air. A normal film does not exclude perforation.
Ultrasound first for right upper quadrant and pelvic pain; CT with contrast when the diagnosis remains unclear and the patient is stable enough to travel.
ECG in anyone over 50 or with epigastric pain: inferior myocardial infarction presents as an abdomen.

sources.title: Guidelines for the management of intra-abdominal infections

investigate.text: Erect chest radiograph, then CT with contrast if stable and the film is normal but suspicion persists.
Lactate, arterial or venous blood gas, full blood count, U&E, coagulation, group and crossmatch.
Blood cultures before antibiotics where taking them will not delay the first dose.
Score severity to guide the level of post-operative care, not the decision to operate.

sources.title: Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO)

investigate.text: Examine every hernial orifice and do a rectal examination before ordering anything.
U&E and a venous gas: the metabolic picture of vomiting and third-spacing drives resuscitation.
CT with contrast defines level, cause and any transition point, and is the test that finds a closed loop.
Water-soluble contrast study in adhesive small-bowel obstruction is both prognostic and often therapeutic.
Serial lactate if strangulation is a possibility. A rising lactate in this setting is a decision, not a data point.

sources.title: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18): diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis

investigate.text: Ultrasound is first-line: wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, stones, and a sonographic Murphy sign.
FBC, CRP, LFT, amylase. A rising bilirubin or alkaline phosphatase points at the duct, not the gallbladder.
MRCP when the duct is suspected and the picture is not frank cholangitis.
Grade severity formally: it changes whether this is an early cholecystectomy, a drainage, or an intensive-care admission.

sources.title: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18): diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholangitis

investigate.text: Blood cultures before the first antibiotic dose: bacteraemia is common and the isolate changes therapy.
LFT, coagulation, lactate, FBC, U&E.
Ultrasound first; MRCP or endoscopic ultrasound when the level of obstruction is unclear.
Grade severity formally. Grade III is the trigger for urgent drainage rather than a planned one.

sources.title: Guidelines for the management of intra-abdominal infections

investigate.text: Ultrasound then contrast CT to size, count and localise. Left-lobe and subcapsular collections behave differently.
Amoebic serology alongside blood cultures. In India the pyogenic-versus-amoebic split changes the whole plan.
Aspirate for culture when drainage is being done anyway; do not aspirate purely for diagnosis in a small abscess responding to therapy.

sources.title: Guidelines for the management of intra-abdominal infections

investigate.text: Daily abdominal radiograph while the colon is dilated: transverse colonic diameter is the number surgery tracks.
Stool culture and Clostridioides difficile testing before assuming inflammatory bowel disease.
CRP, albumin, lactate, FBC daily. A falling albumin with a rising CRP is the deterioration nobody notices.
CT if perforation, abscess or ischaemia is suspected.

sources.title: Guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias

investigate.text: Clinical diagnosis. Imaging is for doubt, not for confirmation of an obvious irreducible tender lump.
CT when the lump is equivocal, obese habitus, or a Richter or obturator hernia is possible.
Lactate, FBC, U&E and group and save if there is any suspicion of compromised bowel.

sources.title: Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections

investigate.text: This is a clinical and operative diagnosis. Do not delay exploration for any test.
Bloods and lactate are for resuscitation and critical-care planning, not for deciding whether to operate.
Imaging only if it will not delay theatre and the diagnosis is genuinely uncertain. Gas on a film supports the diagnosis; its absence excludes nothing.

sources.title: Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections

investigate.text: Pus for culture at the time of drainage. A surface swab of intact skin answers a different question.
Ultrasound when fluctuance is uncertain, the collection is deep, or the patient is obese.
MRI for suspected ischiorectal, supralevator or horseshoe extension of a perianal abscess.
Capillary glucose and HbA1c: an abscess is often how diabetes presents.

sources.title: Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections

investigate.text: Mark the margin with a pen and date it. That single act is worth more than most of the bloods.
Ultrasound if a drainable collection is possible: antibiotics do not drain an abscess.
Blood cultures only when systemically unwell, immunocompromised, or after immersion or animal exposure.
Look for the portal of entry - interdigital tinea, a venous ulcer, a bite - and treat it, or it recurs.

sources.title: Global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection, 2nd edition

investigate.text: Deep specimen at the time of opening or drainage. A superficial swab grows colonisers and misdirects therapy.
Ultrasound or CT for a suspected deep or organ-space collection: the outside can look almost normal.
CRP trend after day three is the most useful single number in post-operative infection.
Glucose control and nutritional status are part of the investigation, not an afterthought.

sources.org: International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF) / IDSA
sources.title: Guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diabetes-related foot infections

investigate.text: Probe-to-bone at the bedside, then a plain radiograph; MRI when osteomyelitis is suspected and the film is normal.
Assess perfusion in every case: pedal pulses, ankle-brachial index, toe pressures. Infection does not clear an ischaemic foot.
Deep tissue or bone specimen for culture, not a superficial swab.
HbA1c, renal function and albumin. Renal function also decides the antibiotic dose.
